title: Validation Gates, Canary Releases & Model Serving
summary: Build the release path for a model: a validation gate that blocks overall, per-slice and latency regressions, a deterministic canary router, a canary analysis that knows when it has enough evidence, and a tiny batching model server that validates its inputs.

hints.test_percentile_nearest_rank: Sort the values. The nearest-rank p-th percentile is the value at 1-based rank ceil(q·n/100), with a minimum rank of 1. It always returns one of the observed values, with no interpolation.
hints.test_gate_overall_checks: Fail 'min_metric:<metric>' when the candidate is below min_metric, and 'regression:<metric>' when production − candidate > max_regression. Landing exactly on the tolerance passes.
hints.test_gate_catches_slice_regression: A better overall number can hide a broken segment. Walk production's slices in sorted order. A slice missing from the candidate is 'missing_slice:<name>', and a drop larger than the slice tolerance is 'slice_regression:<name>'.
hints.test_gate_latency_budget_uses_percentile: Compute the nearest-rank percentile (latency_percentile, default 95) of candidate['latencies_ms'] and compare it with the budget. Don't use the mean or the max, and don't sort the caller's list in place.
hints.test_bucket_is_stable_sha256: Python's built-in hash() of a string is randomized per process, so it can't be used for routing. Use hashlib.sha256(str(request_id).encode('utf-8')), take the first 8 bytes as a big-endian int, then take it mod buckets.
hints.test_route_percentages_and_sticky: A request goes to canary when bucket(request_id) < canary_percent * BUCKETS / 100. A fixed threshold on a stable bucket makes routing sticky, and raising the percentage only adds users. Reject percentages outside [0, 100].
hints.test_canary_decision: Compare error rates (errors / requests). Roll back when canary_rate − baseline_rate > max_increase, otherwise promote. errors > requests is invalid input.
hints.test_canary_waits_for_min_samples: Before deciding anything, check that both arms have at least min_samples requests. If either has fewer, return 'continue'. A handful of requests is noise, not evidence.
hints.test_server_batches_preserve_order: Validate every request first and remember its original index. Send only valid rows to the model in chunks of max_batch_size, keeping arrival order, and write each prediction back to results[index].
hints.test_server_schema_validation: Check for a dict, missing keys, unexpected keys, and types: bools are never numbers, 'int' needs an int, and 'float' accepts int or float but only finite ones. Invalid requests never reach the model. A model that returns the wrong number of predictions should raise RuntimeError.
